domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

questions.title: Org-wide control that covers future projects
questions.summary: IAM and org policy are inherited downward, so binding at the organisation node covers all current and future descendants.
questions.question: A new security standard must apply to every project your company owns, including projects that will be created next year. You want to configure it once and not revisit it. At which level of the resource hierarchy should you act?

options.A: Apply the configuration at the folder containing the affected projects.
options.B: Apply the configuration at the organisation node.
options.C: Apply the configuration on each individual project.
options.D: Apply the configuration directly on the individual resource.

explanation.summary: IAM policies and organisation policies are inherited down the hierarchy, so a binding at the organisation node automatically covers every current and future descendant.

option_breakdown.A: A folder scopes the setting to one branch of the hierarchy — wrong when the requirement is company-wide, and wrong when it must apply to exactly one project.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. IAM policies and organisation policies are inherited down the hierarchy, so a binding at the organisation node automatically covers every current and future descendant.
option_breakdown.C: Per-project configuration does not inherit to projects created later, so it drifts as the estate grows and multiplies the administrative effort.
option_breakdown.D: Resource-level configuration is the narrowest scope available and cannot express an inheritance rule for a group of projects.

questions.title: Departmental access boundary
questions.summary: A folder is the inheritance boundary for a department: bind once, and every current and future child project inherits.
questions.question: The finance department's projects — and only those — must share one set of access controls. Finance creates new projects each quarter and expects them to pick up the same controls automatically, without affecting other departments. What should you do?

options.A: Tag every finance resource with a label and write an IAM condition on the label in each project.
options.B: Grant the finance groups their roles at the organisation node.
options.C: Create a Finance folder, move the finance projects into it, and grant the roles on the folder.
options.D: Grant the roles on each finance project, and add them to every new finance project as it is created.

explanation.summary: A folder is the inheritance boundary for a department: one binding covers every current and future project in it and nothing outside it.

option_breakdown.A: Labels are not an IAM control — conditions use resource-manager tags or names, not labels — and per-project conditions still have to be repeated.
option_breakdown.B: An organisation grant reaches every department, which breaks the “only finance” boundary.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A folder is the inheritance boundary for a department: one binding covers every current and future project in it and nothing outside it.
option_breakdown.D: Per-project grants do not reach projects created next quarter unless someone remembers to add them.

questions.title: Isolating regulated workloads
questions.summary: A dedicated folder gives regulated projects a single inheritance point and makes the compliance boundary explicit.
questions.question: Workloads that process regulated data must be separated from the rest of the estate so a stricter set of controls can be inherited by every project holding that data, and so the compliance boundary is visible in the hierarchy itself. How should you structure this?

options.A: Apply the configuration on each individual project.
options.B: Apply the configuration directly on the individual resource.
options.C: Apply the configuration at the organisation node.
options.D: Apply the configuration at the folder containing the affected projects.

explanation.summary: Grouping the regulated projects under a dedicated folder creates a single inheritance point for the stricter controls and makes the compliance boundary explicit in the hierarchy.

option_breakdown.A: Per-project configuration does not inherit to projects created later, so it drifts as the estate grows and multiplies the administrative effort.
option_breakdown.B: Resource-level configuration is the narrowest scope available and cannot express an inheritance rule for a group of projects.
option_breakdown.C: The organisation node scopes a setting to every project the company owns, which is broader than a departmental or single-project requirement and awkward to carve exceptions out of.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Grouping the regulated projects under a dedicated folder creates a single inheritance point for the stricter controls and makes the compliance boundary explicit in the hierarchy.

questions.title: Organisation-wide asset visibility for auditors
questions.summary: Only an organisation-node binding gives visibility across all folders and projects, including ones created later.
questions.question: Auditors must be able to inventory every resource the company runs, wherever it sits in the hierarchy, without anyone having to remember to grant them access to newly created folders. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the auditors' group roles/cloudasset.viewer on every project today, and add it to each new project as it is created.
options.B: Grant the auditors' group roles/cloudasset.viewer on the largest folder, where most projects live.
options.C: Grant the auditors' group roles/cloudasset.viewer at the organisation node.
options.D: Export an Asset Inventory snapshot to a bucket each month and share the bucket with the auditors.

explanation.summary: A binding at the organisation inherits to every folder and project, including ones created later, and Cloud Asset Viewer lets the auditors search and export the whole inventory.

option_breakdown.A: Per-project grants must be repeated for every new project — exactly the step the requirement says nobody should have to remember.
option_breakdown.B: A folder grant leaves every project outside that folder invisible, so the inventory is incomplete.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A binding at the organisation inherits to every folder and project, including ones created later, and Cloud Asset Viewer lets the auditors search and export the whole inventory.
option_breakdown.D: A monthly export is stale between runs and gives no live search; it also creates a copy to secure.

questions.title: Block public IPs except on a bastion
questions.summary: compute.vmExternalIpAccess is a list constraint: deny by default, allow-list the bastion.
questions.question: Engineers keep attaching external IP addresses to development VMs. Security wants that blocked everywhere except in one bastion project, and wants the block enforced at creation time rather than caught in review. Which organisation policy constraint should you enforce?

options.A: constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains
options.B: constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
options.C: constraints/gcp.resourceLocations
options.D: constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess

explanation.summary: compute.vmExternalIpAccess is a list constraint that denies external IPs by default and can allow-list specific instances, which is exactly the bastion exception pattern.

option_breakdown.A: Domain restricted sharing limits which identity domains may appear in IAM policies; it does not restrict how resources are configured.
option_breakdown.B: This constraint blocks creation of user-managed service account keys; it has no effect on networking, storage or location.
option_breakdown.C: Resource Location Restriction limits the regions in which resources may be created; it does not control identity or networking behaviour.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. compute.vmExternalIpAccess is a list constraint that denies external IPs by default and can allow-list specific instances, which is exactly the bastion exception pattern.

options.B: constraints/gcp.resourceLocations
options.C: constraints/compute.requireShieldedVm
options.D: constraints/storage.publicAccessPrevention

questions.title: Link projects without seeing spend
questions.summary: Billing Account User is exactly the link-projects permission, with no read access to cost data.
questions.question: A team lead must be able to attach newly created projects to the central billing account, but company policy says they must not be able to see the organisation's spend. Which role should you grant, following least privilege?

options.A: Grant the Billing Account Administrator role on the billing account.
options.B: Grant the Billing Account User role on the billing account.
options.C: Grant the Billing Account Viewer role on the billing account.
options.D: Grant the Project Billing Manager role on the project.

explanation.summary: Billing Account User is precisely the link-projects permission with no read access to cost data, which is the least-privilege answer for this task.

option_breakdown.A: Billing Account Administrator can link and unlink projects, manage billing users and close the account — far more than a read-only or single-task need.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Billing Account User is precisely the link-projects permission with no read access to cost data, which is the least-privilege answer for this task.
option_breakdown.C: Billing Account Viewer is read-only on billing data; it cannot link projects or change budgets, so it fails any requirement involving modification.
option_breakdown.D: Project Billing Manager lets a principal change which billing account a project uses, with no rights over the billing account's own data or settings.

questions.title: Threshold alerts at 50/90/100 percent
questions.summary: A budget scoped to the project with multiple threshold rules emails the billing recipients.
questions.question: Finance wants to be emailed when monthly spend on the analytics project reaches 50%, 90% and 100% of its allocation. What should you configure?

options.A: Create a Cloud Billing budget that publishes threshold notifications to a Pub/Sub topic consumed by a Cloud Run function.
options.B: Enable Cloud Billing export to BigQuery and query it.
options.C: Create a Cloud Billing budget with threshold rules that notify by email.
options.D: Apply labels to resources and group costs by label in billing reports.

explanation.summary: A Cloud Billing budget scoped to the project with multiple threshold rules sends exactly these percentage-based notifications to the billing account's email recipients.

option_breakdown.A: Routing to Pub/Sub is only warranted when an automated reaction is required; it is unnecessary complexity when people simply need to be told.
option_breakdown.B: Billing export gives detailed after-the-fact analysis with hours of latency; it is not an alerting mechanism.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A Cloud Billing budget scoped to the project with multiple threshold rules sends exactly these percentage-based notifications to the billing account's email recipients.
option_breakdown.D: Labels make cost attribution possible but generate no notification and enforce no threshold.

questions.title: Automatically stop a sandbox over budget
questions.summary: Budget notifications on Pub/Sub can trigger a function that calls the Compute Engine API.
questions.question: When a sandbox project passes its budget, the company wants automation to shut down its VMs rather than simply send an email to someone who may be asleep. How should you wire this?

options.A: Apply labels to resources and group costs by label in billing reports.
options.B: Reduce the project's quotas to cap consumption.
options.C: Create a Cloud Billing budget with threshold rules that notify by email.
options.D: Create a Cloud Billing budget that publishes threshold notifications to a Pub/Sub topic consumed by a Cloud Run function.

explanation.summary: Budget notifications published to Pub/Sub can trigger a Cloud Run function that calls the Compute Engine API, which is the supported pattern for automated cost response.

option_breakdown.A: Labels make cost attribution possible but generate no notification and enforce no threshold.
option_breakdown.B: Quotas limit how many resources can exist, not how much they cost, and lowering them breaks legitimate scaling rather than tracking spend.
option_breakdown.C: Email threshold notifications inform people but take no action, so they cannot satisfy a requirement to react programmatically.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Budget notifications published to Pub/Sub can trigger a Cloud Run function that calls the Compute Engine API, which is the supported pattern for automated cost response.

questions.title: Alert on forecast rather than actual spend
questions.summary: Budgets support a forecasted-spend threshold basis, firing on the projected total.
questions.question: A department wants a single warning when its *forecasted* month-end spend is on track to exceed its allocation, rather than waiting until the money is already spent. What should you configure?

options.A: Create a budget for the department's projects with a threshold rule on forecasted spend at 100%.
options.B: Create a budget with threshold rules on actual spend at 90% and 100%.
options.C: Lower the department's Compute Engine quotas to match its allocation.
options.D: Schedule a monthly query over the billing export that compares spend with the allocation.

explanation.summary: A threshold rule with the forecasted-spend basis fires when the projected month-end total crosses the amount — before the money is spent.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A threshold rule with the forecasted-spend basis fires when the projected month-end total crosses the amount — before the money is spent.
option_breakdown.B: Actual-spend thresholds fire only once the money has been consumed, which is what the department wants to avoid.
option_breakdown.C: A quota caps capacity and would interrupt workloads; it does not warn anyone about cost.
option_breakdown.D: A monthly query reports after the month has ended — too late to act on a forecast.

questions.title: Active Directory as the source of truth
questions.summary: GCDS reads AD/LDAP on a schedule and creates, updates and suspends the matching Cloud Identity users and groups.
questions.question: Your organisation keeps its authoritative employee list in on-premises Active Directory and wants to keep it that way, while having full control over the Google accounts employees use for all Google services. The same users and groups must exist in Cloud Identity and stay updated as staff change. What should you do?

options.A: Use Google Cloud Directory Sync to provision users and groups from the on-premises directory.
options.B: Configure SAML-based single sign-on between the external identity provider and Cloud Identity.
options.C: Create the accounts manually in the Google Admin console.
options.D: Configure Workforce Identity Federation so users access Google Cloud with their existing identity provider credentials.

explanation.summary: Google Cloud Directory Sync reads Active Directory or LDAP on a schedule and creates, updates and suspends the matching Cloud Identity users and groups, keeping the directory authoritative on-premises while the accounts stay fully managed.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Google Cloud Directory Sync reads Active Directory or LDAP on a schedule and creates, updates and suspends the matching Cloud Identity users and groups, keeping the directory authoritative on-premises while the accounts stay fully managed.
option_breakdown.B: SSO governs authentication only. It creates no accounts and keeps no group membership in step, so on its own it cannot solve a provisioning problem.
option_breakdown.C: Manual account creation does not scale, drifts from the source of truth, and leaves deprovisioning to human memory.
option_breakdown.D: Workforce Identity Federation grants access to external identities without Cloud Identity accounts at all; it does not populate a directory or manage licences.

explanation.gcloud_command: ./sync-cmd -a -c config.xml   # scheduled; GCDS is configured with Configuration Manager

questions.title: API not enabled on a new project

options.A: Request an increase for the affected quota.
options.B: Enable the required API on the project.
options.C: Grant the caller the appropriate IAM role.
options.D: Add exponential backoff with jitter to the client.

explanation.summary: Newly created projects have most APIs disabled by default; the error names the service, and enabling it on the project is the direct fix.

option_breakdown.A: A quota increase raises a capacity ceiling. It is the wrong remedy for a service that is not enabled, or for a permission error.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Newly created projects have most APIs disabled by default; the error names the service, and enabling it on the project is the direct fix.
option_breakdown.C: An IAM role fixes a permission denial, not a disabled service or an exhausted quota.
option_breakdown.D: Backoff smooths transient rate limiting but cannot create capacity the quota does not allow, nor enable a service.

questions.title: Regional CPU limit reached at peak
questions.summary: Regional CPU limits are quotas; request an increase for that quota in that region.
questions.question: A batch job fails at peak because the project has hit its regional limit on CPUs. The workload's demand is legitimate and cannot be reduced. What should you do?

options.B: Create the resources in an additional project to spread the load.
options.C: Request an increase for the affected quota.
options.D: Enable the required API on the project.

explanation.summary: Regional CPU limits are quotas; when the demand is legitimate the supported remedy is to request an increase for that specific quota in that region.

option_breakdown.A: Backoff smooths transient rate limiting but cannot create capacity the quota does not allow, nor enable a service.
option_breakdown.B: Splitting across projects is a workaround for per-project quotas, not a fix for a disabled API or an insufficient role, and it fragments the estate.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Regional CPU limits are quotas; when the demand is legitimate the supported remedy is to request an increase for that specific quota in that region.
option_breakdown.D: Enabling an API makes a service callable in the project; it does nothing about capacity limits or permissions.

questions.title: Intermittent 429s during short spikes

option_breakdown.B: A quota increase raises a capacity ceiling. It is the wrong remedy for a service that is not enabled, or for a permission error.
option_breakdown.C: An IAM role fixes a permission denial, not a disabled service or an exhausted quota.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Rate-limit errors on brief spikes are the documented case for exponential backoff with jitter; the underlying quota is adequate.

# client-side retry; inspect limits with:
gcloud services quota list --service=SERVICE --consumer=projects/PROJECT_ID

questions.title: Pipeline prerequisite for a fresh project
questions.summary: Service enablement is an idempotent prerequisite that belongs at the start of the pipeline.
questions.question: Before a Terraform run can create Cloud Run services in a fresh project, the pipeline must guarantee the necessary services are available, and the step must be safe to run on every execution. What should the pipeline do first?

options.A: Run gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com (and the other APIs it needs) as the pipeline's first step.
options.B: Grant the pipeline's service account roles/owner on the project.
options.C: Ask an administrator to enable the APIs in the console before each run.
options.D: Retry the Terraform run until the services become available.

explanation.summary: Owner would let the pipeline enable APIs but does not enable them, and it is far broader than needed.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Enabling an API is idempotent — it succeeds whether or not the API is already on — so it is safe on every run and guarantees the prerequisite. (Terraform's google_project_service does the same declaratively.)
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Owner would let the pipeline enable APIs but does not enable them, and it is far broader than needed.
option_breakdown.C: A manual console step is not repeatable and cannot be guaranteed on every execution.
option_breakdown.D: A disabled API never becomes available by itself; retrying only repeats the failure.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com

questions.title: Survive one data centre failure
questions.summary: Zones are independent failure domains inside a region; a regional MIG spreads instances across them.
questions.question: A web tier must stay available if a single Google Cloud data centre fails. The business explicitly accepts an outage if an entire region is lost, and wants to avoid cross-region cost and latency. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy across multiple regions.
options.B: Deploy into a single zone.
options.C: Deploy across multiple zones within a single region.
options.D: Verify the product's availability in the target location before committing to the design.

explanation.summary: Zones are independent failure domains inside a region, so spreading instances across zones — via a regional managed instance group — survives a zonal failure at no cross-region latency cost.

option_breakdown.A: Multi-region costs more and adds cross-region latency and consistency complexity; it is overkill when only zone-level redundancy is required.
option_breakdown.B: A single zone has no redundancy: a zonal failure takes the workload down entirely.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Zones are independent failure domains inside a region, so spreading instances across zones — via a regional managed instance group — survives a zonal failure at no cross-region latency cost.
option_breakdown.D: Checking availability is a planning step; it provides no redundancy and reduces no latency by itself.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute instance-groups managed create web-mig \
  --template=web-tpl --size=6 --region=us-central1

questions.title: Find every VM with an external IP now

questions.title: Locate a bucket by partial name
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Asset search matches resources by name fragment across the organisation.
questions.question: An engineer needs to find which project owns a Cloud Storage bucket, knowing only part of its name. What should they do?

options.A: Run gcloud storage ls in every project until the bucket appears.
options.B: Search for the bucket in Cloud Asset Inventory across the organisation by name fragment.
options.C: Read the billing export for the storage SKU charges.
options.D: Search Admin Activity audit logs for bucket creation events.

explanation.summary: Audit logs are kept for a limited time and record changes; a bucket created years ago may not appear.

option_breakdown.A: Listing project by project is slow and needs access to each project; it is the manual version of a search the platform already provides.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. gcloud asset search-all-resources (or the console's Asset Inventory search) matches a name fragment across the organisation and returns the full resource name, including the project.
option_breakdown.C: Billing data is aggregated by project and SKU, not by bucket name.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Audit logs are kept for a limited time and record changes; a bucket created years ago may not appear.

questions.title: Centralise logs from every project
questions.summary: An aggregated sink at the org or folder node routes descendants' logs to one destination.
questions.question: Security wants every project's logs delivered into one central location for retention and search, configured once at the organisation level rather than per project. What should you do?

options.A: Install the Ops Agent on the virtual machines.
options.B: Create aggregated log sinks routing every project's logs into one central log bucket.
options.C: Configure a metrics scope in one project and add the other projects to it.
options.D: View each project's dashboards separately in its own Cloud Monitoring page.

explanation.summary: An aggregated sink created at the organisation or folder node, with the include-children flag, routes logs from every descendant project to a single destination and keeps working for projects created later.

option_breakdown.A: The Ops Agent collects guest-level metrics and logs from VMs; it does not consolidate anything across projects.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. An aggregated sink created at the organisation or folder node, with the include-children flag, routes logs from every descendant project to a single destination and keeps working for projects created later.
option_breakdown.C: A metrics scope consolidates observability across projects for viewing; it is not a log destination and not an agent.
option_breakdown.D: Per-project views are the default and are exactly what a consolidation requirement asks you to replace.

option_breakdown.A: Per-project views are the default and are exactly what a consolidation requirement asks you to replace.

questions.title: Console access for an external workforce

options.B: Create service account keys and distribute them to the external system.
options.C: Create a Cloud Identity account for every external user.
options.D: Configure Workforce Identity Federation with a workforce pool and provider.

explanation.summary: Workforce Identity Federation federates human identities from an external IdP into Google Cloud, giving console and gcloud access through a workforce pool without provisioning Cloud Identity accounts.

option_breakdown.D: Correct. Workforce Identity Federation federates human identities from an external IdP into Google Cloud, giving console and gcloud access through a workforce pool without provisioning Cloud Identity accounts.

questions.title: An organisation without a domain for a new Free Trial customer

questions.question: A two-person startup signs up for Google Cloud for the first time on a new Free Trial. They own no company domain and have no Cloud Identity or Google Workspace account, but want folders, organisation policies and organisation-level IAM from the first day. options.A: Buy a domain, verify it in Cloud Identity Free, and wait for the organisation to be created from it.
options.B: Use the standalone organisation that is created for the new Free Trial sign-up; the signing-up user becomes its Organization Owner.
options.C: Create a top-level folder in the console, which becomes the organisation node for the account.
options.D: Open a support case asking Google to provision an organisation for their Gmail account.

explanation.summary: A standalone organisation gives a new Free Trial customer a real resource hierarchy — folders, organisation policies, organisation-level IAM — without a verified domain or a Cloud Identity super administrator. It is created automatically at sign-up and the user who signed up becomes Organization Owner.

option_breakdown.A: Verifying a domain works, but they own no domain; the guide's standalone route exists precisely for this case.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The organisation is named after the user rather than a domain, and other people join by invitation.
option_breakdown.C: Folders live under an organisation; creating one never creates the organisation itself.
option_breakdown.D: Organisations are not provisioned by support request; they come from Cloud Identity/Workspace or a standalone sign-up.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud organizations list   # the standalone organisation appears, named after the user

questions.title: A second owner for a standalone organisation

option_breakdown.B: Standalone organisations exist for customers without Cloud Identity; they hold Google accounts and workforce pool principals.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Invitations and a second human owner are the supported way to share ownership; service accounts are excluded.
option_breakdown.D: Workforce identity pools federate sign-in from an external IdP; membership grants no role on its own.

questions.title: Plain-language questions about your own resources
